main_text.p: animalium carnes alienas esse, praefertim pan-theraram [?] leonum, arbitrandum est, nam Leonis tradunt tantum esse virus, ut halitus sue odorem cibis foedum relinquat, eoq, profciffe [?] interiora ejus graviffime olent: flatus prae-rea emittit acerrimos, urinamque graviter o-lentem, quemadmodum tefantur, quiin Magnorum Principum aulis Leonum domiterunt fuerunt cuftodes.

Orientis gentes quasdam, ut Battros, Camelorum carnibus vesci certum est. Aristoteles lac as carnes camelorum omnium fauiffimae effe teftatus eft, qui tamen locus eruditiorbus quibusdam fwpectus eft, ut Hieron, Mercuriali variar. Lett.l. 2. putat enim ab aliquo ex marginibus interferta, tum etiam quod Plinius l. 28. folum lac non carnes Camelorum ab hominum lacte facit dulciffimum. Ac de lacte convenit inter omnes. Galenus 3. de aliment. carnes camelinas valde damnat.

Solinus c. 52. scribit lutulentas aquas Camelos captare, refugere puras, nifi cœnofior fuerit liquor, affidua conculcatione limum excitare, ut turbetur, quod vel maxime ab illorum efe aliquem deterrere debeat.

page.notes: The small marks ("e") printed before some lines (at "Aristoteles", "Ac de lacte", "Antiphanes") are doubtful; they may be marginal reference signs and were not transcribed as notes. "therarum [?]" is an uncertain symbol, as is "profciffe [?]". The catchword is partly cut off and marked as doubtful. The lower-left mark is only a print fragment and was left out.
